reason: The instructions call for lining the binding boards with paper, so I’ll place the planks at the library table.
expectation: The planks will be positioned for adding paper, though I’m not sure whether that is the required order.

alternatives.reason: Placing the paper first might also prepare the lining, but the planks seem like the natural base.

effect: The planks are at the library table, and paper can now be combined with them there.
reason: The chapter calls for lining the binding boards with paper, and this option directly fits that instruction.
expectation: The paper will line the planks to prepare the binding boards.

effect: The lined binding boards have four slots, one for each set of studies.
reaction: The empty slots make the remaining task clear.
reason: I'll add the botanical sheets first to fill the plants slot.
expectation: The botanical sheets will fit into the plants slot on the boards.

effect: The botanical sheets are fitted, leaving the pond, weather and stars studies to add.
reason: I'll add the pond drawings to fill another study slot.
expectation: The pond drawings will fit into the binding boards.

effect: The pond drawings are fitted, leaving the weather and stars studies.
reason: I'll add the weather record to fill another slot.
expectation: The weather record will fit into the binding boards.

effect: The weather record is fitted, leaving the star chart as the last study.
reason: The star chart is the only remaining study and the only offered combination.
expectation: The star chart will fit into the boards and complete the collection of four studies.

effect: All four studies are gathered, and the remaining goal is to bind the encyclopedia.
reaction: The final study fitted as expected.
reason: Thread is the only offered combination and should stitch the gathered studies into a volume.
expectation: The thread will bind the boards and studies into an encyclopedia.

effect: The thread bound the four studies into an encyclopedia, completing the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the earlier studies gathered into a usable volume.

mostWorthwhile.text: Binding the encyclopedia was the most worthwhile action: it brought the gathered studies together and explained how they could be used.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the studies one at a time felt repetitive once the slots and the process were clear.

surprise.text: The lined boards revealed named slots for all four studies, making the structure of the volume explicit.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; placing the planks and lining them followed the chapter instructions.

continue.text: I might continue to see how the collected knowledge is used, though the repeated fittings offered little meaningful choice.
